method: PHASE (A: reviewed branch -> PR | B: approved PR -> merge/deploy/canary) x ARRIVAL (explicit | implicit | contextual). Positives cover both phases and all three arrival styles, including the founder's own phrasing of the job ("finito il lavoro, arriva la PR, /ship"). Negatives are the adjacent doors this skill must not steal: the merge-readiness verdict itself (real-testing), the code-quality read of a diff (review), launch planning with flags and staged rollout (shipping-and-launch), destructive git and worktree hygiene (git-power), and the two cases the skill's own 'Quando NON usarla' names — an unreviewed branch and a static design-mockup deploy.

cases.prompt: Run ship on this reviewed branch: redaction scan, version bump, changelog entry, then open the PR.
The branch is reviewed and green. Get it to a PR the way this repo expects, and make sure the version and CHANGELOG are not left behind again.
Ho finito il lavoro, sono arrivato alla PR. Fammi tutta la cerimonia di questa repo.
PR #901 is approved and the checks are green. Merge it safely and deploy, then watch the canary.
This PR has been sitting for two days waiting on a click. Land it and get prod onto the new commit.
Last time we retried gh pr merge blind after a failure and ended up with four conflicting merges. Do it properly this time.
Deploy this branch to staging, prove it there, comment the verdict on the PR, then merge and put it in prod.
Is this diff mergeable? Derive the perimeter from the change and exercise every new branch before you answer.
Read this diff against our coding standards and against what the originating issue asked for, and report the two axes separately.
We launch the new pricing page next week. Plan the feature flag, the staged rollout percentages and the rollback criteria.
I have 25 stale worktrees and a handful of branches nobody remembers. Clean them up without losing uncommitted work.
Nobody has looked at this branch yet, but push it up as a PR anyway so I can see it in GitHub.
Put this static HTML mockup on a Vercel preview so the stakeholder can look at it tomorrow.
